sanskrit: agniṃ brūmo vanaspatīn oṣadhīr uta vīrudhaḥ | indraṃ bṛhaspatiṃ sūryaṃ te no muñcantv aṃhasaḥ ||
english: We invoke Agni, the lords of the forest, the healing plants, and the creeping herbs; Indra, Bṛhaspati, and Sūrya — may they release us from distress.

sanskrit: brūmo devaṃ savitāraṃ dhātāram uta pūṣaṇam | tvaṣṭāram agryaṃ brūmas te (…) ||
english: We invoke the divine Savitṛ, Dhātṛ, and Pūṣan; Tvaṣṭṛ, the foremost, we invoke — may they release us from distress.

sanskrit: brūmo rājānaṃ varuṇaṃ mitraṃ viṣṇum atho bhagam | aṃśaṃ vivasvantaṃ brūmas te (…) ||
english: We invoke the king Varuṇa, Mitra, Viṣṇu, and also Bhaga; Aṃśa and Vivasvat we invoke — may they release us from distress.

sanskrit: gandharvāpsaraso brūmo aśvinā brahmaṇaspatim | aryamā nāma yo devas te (…) ||
english: We invoke the Gandharvas and the Apsarases, the twin Aśvins, and Brahmaṇaspati; the god whose name is Aryaman — may they release us from distress.

sanskrit: vātaṃ brūmaḥ parjanyam antarikṣam atho diśaḥ | āśāś ca sarvā brūmas te (…) ||
english: We invoke Vāta, Parjanya, the atmosphere, and the directions; all the quarters too we invoke — may they release us from distress.

sanskrit: ahorātre idaṃ brūma sūryācandramasā ubhā | ādityān sarvān brūmas te no muñcantv aṃhasaḥ ||
english: Day and night we invoke here; both Sūrya and Candramās; all the Ādityas we invoke — may they release us from distress.

sanskrit: muñcantu mā śapathyād ahorātre atho uṣāḥ | somo mā divyo muñcatu yam āhuś candramā iti ||
english: May Day and Night release me from the curse, and also Dawn; may the celestial Soma release me — he whom they call Candramās.

sanskrit: pañca rājyāni vīrudhāṃ somaśreṣṭhāni brūmasi | bhaṅgo darbho yavaḥ sahas te no muñcantv aṃhasaḥ ||
english: The five kingdoms of plants, with Soma as their chief, we proclaim — hemp, darbha-grass, barley, and sahas — may they release us from distress.

sanskrit: ye grāmyāḥ sapta paśava āraṇyā uta ye mṛgāḥ | śakuntān pakṣiṇo brūmas te no muñcantv aṃhasaḥ ||
english: The seven domestic animals and whatever wild beasts roam the forest; the birds and the winged ones we invoke — may they release us from distress.

sanskrit: bhavāśarvāv idaṃ brūma ugraḥ paśupatiś ca yaḥ | iṣūr yā eṣāṃ vidmas te no muñcantv aṃhasaḥ ||
english: We invoke here Bhava and Śarva, the fierce one and he who is lord of cattle; the arrows of theirs that we know of — may they release us from distress.

sanskrit: yajñaṃ brūmo yajamānam ṛcaḥ sāmāni bheṣajā | yajūṃṣi hotrān brūmas te no muñcantv aṃhasaḥ ||
english: We invoke the sacrifice and the sacrificer, the ṛc-verses, the sāmans as healing powers; the yajus-formulas and the hotṛ-priests we invoke — may they release us from distress.

sanskrit: ṛtūn brūma ṛtupatīn ārtavām̐ uta hāyanān | samāḥ saṃvatsarān māsas te no (…) ||
english: We invoke the seasons and the lords of the seasons, the seasonal plants and the yearly ones; years, full years, and months — may they release us from distress.

sanskrit: divaṃ brūmo nakṣatrāṇi bhūmiṃ yakṣāṇi parvatān | samudrā nadyo veśantās te (…) ||
english: We invoke the sky, the lunar mansions, the earth, the yakṣas, and the mountains; the oceans, the rivers, and the streams — may they release us from distress.

sanskrit: sapta ṛṣīn vā idaṃ brūmo 'po devīḥ prajāpatim | pitṝn yamaśreṣṭhān brūmas te (…) ||
english: The seven seers we invoke here, the divine waters, and Prajāpati; the Fathers with Yama as their chief we invoke — may they release us from distress.

sanskrit: viśvān devān idaṃ brūmaḥ satyasandhān ṛtāvṛdhaḥ | viśvābhiḥ patnībhiḥ sākaṃ te (…) ||
english: All the gods we invoke here, true to their bonds, those who grow great through sacred order; together with all their consorts — may they release us from distress.

sanskrit: ādityā rudrā vasavo devā daivā atharvaṇaḥ | aṅgiraso manīṣiṇas te (…) ||
english: The Ādityas, the Rudras, the Vasus, the divine Atharvans among the gods; the Aṅgirases, those of inspired wisdom — may they release us from distress.

sanskrit: ye devā diviṣado 'ntarikṣasadaś ca ye | pṛthivyāṃ śakrā ye śritās te (…) ||
english: Those gods who dwell in heaven, and those who dwell in the atmosphere; those mighty ones who are established upon the earth — may they release us from distress.

sanskrit: eta devā dakṣiṇataḥ paśvāt prāñca ud etana purastāc chakrā uttarād viśve devāḥ sametya te (…) ||
english: These gods — rise up eastward from the south, you mighty ones from the east and from the north; all gods assembling together — may they release us from distress.

sanskrit: arāyān brūmo rakṣāṃsi sarpān puṇyajanān uta | mṛtyūn ekaśataṃ brūmas te no muñcantv aṃhasaḥ ||
english: We invoke the arāyas, the rākṣasas, the serpents, and the puṇyajanas; the hundred and one deaths we invoke — may they release us from distress.

sanskrit: yā devīḥ pañca pradiśo ye devā dvādaśartavaḥ | saṃvatsarasya ye daṃṣṭrās te naḥ santu sadā śivāḥ ||
english: The five divine directions and the twelve divine seasons; those who are the fangs of the year — may they always be benign to us.

sanskrit: bhūtaṃ brūmo bhūtapatiṃ bhūtānām uta yas patiḥ | bhūtāni sarvā brūmas te no muñcantv aṃhasaḥ ||
english: We invoke the beings and the lord of beings and him who is master of all beings; all beings in their entirety we invoke — may they release us from distress.

sanskrit: yāvad dyaur yāvat pṛthivī yāvat paryeti sūryaḥ | tāvat tvam ugra oṣadhe pari pāhy arundhati ||
english: As far as the sky extends, as far as the earth extends, as far as the sun moves around — so far do you, O potent plant, protect all around, O Arundhati.

sanskrit: ariṣṭas tvā khanaty ariṣṭāya khanāmi tvā | dvipāc catuṣpād asmākaṃ sarvam astv anāturam ||
english: The uninjured one digs you up; for the sake of freedom from injury I dig you up. May all of our two-footed and four-footed creatures be without disease.

sanskrit: devānām asi svasā marutām asi sañcarī | yaṃ jīvam aśnuṣe tvaṃ na sa riṣyāti pūruṣaḥ ||
english: You are the sister of the gods; you are the companion who moves with the Maruts. Whatever living man you reach, that person shall not suffer harm.

sanskrit: arundhatī nāmāsi tṛtīyasyām ito divi | tatrāmṛtasya rohaṇaṃ tena tvācchāvadāmasi ||
english: Arundhati is your name; you are in the third heaven from here. There is the stalk of immortality — by means of that we call to you.

sanskrit: śaṃ ta āpo hṛdyāḥ śaṃ te kulijyā uta | śaṃ vātaḥ śaṃ bṛhaspatiḥ śaṃ te tapatu sūryaḥ ||
english: Benign to you be the heart-pleasing waters; benign to you the spring-fed streams. Benign be Vāyu, benign Bṛhaspati; may Sūrya warm you with benevolence.

sanskrit: śaṃ ta indrāgnī bhavatāṃ śaṃ rātrī prati dhīyatām | śaṃ te pṛthivyāṃ vīrudhaḥ śam u te santv oṣadhīḥ ||
english: May Indra and Agni be benign to you; may Night be laid down in benevolence. Benign to you be the plants in the earth; benign too may the healing herbs be to you.

sanskrit: bahvīṣu hi tvām avidam oṣadhīṃ vīryavatīm | arundhati tvām āhārṣam ito mā pārayān iti ||
english: Among many plants I have found you, O potent herb; O Arundhati, I have brought you hither — "may she bring us safely across" is what they say.

sanskrit: abhiprepseva jīvantam abhi dasyed arundhatī | eṣā daviddya bheṣajī devī vātīkṛtasya ca ||
english: As if striving to reach a living man, may Arundhati shine forth; this divinely luminous healing goddess cures even him who is afflicted by wind-sickness.

sanskrit: anu ṣiñca nas tat kurv agado vai bhaviṣyati | vātīkṛtasya bheṣajy āgan devy arundhatī ||
english: Sprinkle it upon us, do that — he shall indeed be free of disease. As healer of wind-sickness the divine Arundhati has come.

sanskrit: mā bibher na mariṣyasy agado vai bhaviṣyasi | vātīkṛtasya bheṣajy āgan devy arundhatī ||
english: Fear not — you shall not die; you shall indeed be free of disease. As healer of wind-sickness the divine Arundhati has come.
